name: Perineurioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and immunohistochemical diagnostic criteria for perineurioma

criteria.description: Presence of spindle cells with elongated nuclei arranged in whorled or storiform patterns within nerve fascicles
Positive staining for epithelial membrane antigen (EMA) and claudin-1 with negative S-100 protein
MRI showing fusiform enlargement of peripheral nerve with well-defined margins

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with characteristic immunohistochemical profile (EMA positive, S-100 negative) is required; imaging findings support diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular studies may show deletions in chromosome 22q but are not routinely required.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically affects sensory or mixed nerves

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized motor weakness in affected nerve distribution

common.symptomName: Paresthesia or numbness in affected limb
searchTerms: loss of sensation in arm or leg

common.symptomName: Palpable soft tissue mass along nerve course

searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk in affected area

occasional.symptomName: Reduced deep tendon reflexes in affected limb

searchTerms: localized sweating or heart rate issues

rare.symptomName: Ulceration overlying lesion due to nerve compression
searchTerms: open sore due to nerve compression

imaging: MRI demonstrating fusiform nerve enlargement with homogeneous enhancement
Ultrasound showing hypoechoic nerve swelling with preserved fascicular pattern
genetic: Chromosome 22q deletions or abnormalities reported in some cases
other: Histopathology showing perineurial cell proliferation with EMA positivity and S-100 negativity

distinguishingFeatures: Encapsulated mass separate from nerve fascicles
Different MRI characteristics with target sign
Mixed cellular composition including Schwann cells and fibroblasts

redFlags: Ulceration or skin breakdown over lesion
references: Weiss SW, Goldblum JR. Enzinger and Weiss's Soft Tissue Tumors. 6th ed. 2014.
Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System. 4th ed. 2016.
